# Third-party assets vendored into this repository

Everything the course needs to run is committed here. A bare `git clone` yields a complete,
runnable, fully offline course — there is no download step, and therefore no version drift
between one installation and the next. That property is the whole point of this directory:
a classroom in an air-gapped facility runs exactly the bytes recorded below, forever.

Verify every file at any time:

```bash
bash tools/fetch-vendor.sh --check
```

It recomputes each SHA-384 and compares it against the table in this file. Any mismatch means
the file was truncated, tampered with, or replaced — investigate before teaching from it.

## SHA-384 (base64, same format as an HTML `integrity=` attribute)

```
three.min.js                  sha384-CI3ELBVUz9XQO+97x6nwMDPosPR5XvsxW2ua7N1Xeygeh1IxtgqtCkGfQY9WWdHu
textures/earth_atmos_2048.jpg sha384-CdJTLUEa0xdQcLiyPPAGJYYGIfaqTjvSyDui9elYwNt8kspL5DwbzvhrR4Nw9W4O
textures/moon_1024.jpg        sha384-DefE7ULhs/zJZO2+8xItLwvjjsmGUEPf16LvwNBo7/+HQM5eP54+uppYIM/Qf2Ww
textures/earth_schematic.jpg  sha384-HSo2WNyYo4vOBkidybtsxoS+wN+LGo9j65TVeC5iB9gxOQGYQRxW4qQnpzOGYkJX
textures/moon_schematic.jpg   sha384-74TO4h24Ile8etSWXpdjgpOUahc7WP4KUq1JbFbVsrHmn9VVrHAtb+BZXa1H076/
```

The `three.min.js` hash is the published r128 SRI digest — the same value the course used in its
`integrity=` attribute when it loaded the library from a CDN. Vendoring did not change the bytes.

## three.js — MIT

```
Copyright 2010-2021 Three.js Authors
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
```

MIT permits redistribution provided the copyright notice travels with it; the notice is intact in
the first four lines of `three.min.js` and is reproduced here.

## The photographic planet maps

`earth_atmos_2048.jpg` and `moon_1024.jpg` ship inside the three.js repository's `examples/`
directory and derive from NASA imagery (the Earth map from Blue Marble / Visible Earth). Works
produced by NASA are generally not subject to copyright in the United States and NASA's media
guidelines permit reuse, which is why these are the maps the three.js examples themselves use.

**If your accreditation process requires cleared provenance for every image**, you do not need
them. Delete both files and the course keeps working: `textures.js` resolves each map through a
chain and falls through to the schematic maps below, which we drew ourselves. Nothing else changes.

## Optional: the high-resolution NASA lunar mosaic

`textures/moon_hires.jpg` is **not** in the repository — it is an optional upgrade fetched by
`bash tools/fetch-moon-hires.sh`. When present it leads the Moon texture chain; when absent the
committed 1024x512 map is used and nothing else changes.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Source** | NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, *CGI Moon Kit*, SVS id 4720 — <https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4720> |
| **Data** | LROC Wide Angle Camera natural-colour mosaic, Hapke-normalised, assembled from 100,000+ WAC images; polar gaps filled from LOLA albedo |
| **Sizes** | 2048x1024 (JPEG, 0.4 MB) · 4096x2048 (16-bit TIFF, 12.5 MB) · 8192x4096 (48 MB) |
| **Licence** | NASA imagery is not subject to copyright in the United States. NASA asks for credit. |
| **Credit** | *NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio* — visualizer Ernie Wright (USRA), scientist Noah Petro (NASA/GSFC) |

Why it is optional rather than committed: it is a large binary that most users will not need, and the
course must stay useful with nothing but what we can redistribute freely. It is also **not
hash-pinned** in `fetch-vendor.sh`, because the file is converted locally from a TIFF and the exact
JPEG bytes depend on the Pillow version doing the conversion.

To remove it: `bash tools/fetch-moon-hires.sh --revert`.

## The schematic maps — ours

`earth_schematic.jpg` and `moon_schematic.jpg` are generated procedurally by
`tools/make-textures.py` from a fixed seed, so they are reproducible byte-for-byte. They are
deliberately **schematic, not photographic**: ocean blue with a 15° graticule, a gold equator,
dashed tropics and polar circles, and a green prime meridian.

We chose a coordinate grid over invented continents on purpose. We have no coastline dataset to
draw a truthful Earth offline, and putting fictional geography in front of students training on
orbital mechanics would be worse than showing no geography at all. The grid also teaches: you can
count meridians to watch Earth rotate under an orbit, and read inclination straight off it.

## What is *not* here

Nothing else is needed. The server (`server.js`) has zero dependencies and uses only Node
built-ins, there is no `node_modules`, no build step, and no package manager involved anywhere in
the course. `test/no-external-calls.test.js` enforces the no-outbound-calls property on every
release.
